response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, cu.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS num_orders FROM Customers cu LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id WHERE cu.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.gender), s AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, num_orders, 1.0 * num_orders / NULLIF(SUM(num_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY gender), 0) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT s.*, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT customer_id, gender, num_orders, share, share - avg_share AS gap_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY gap_above_average DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Customers with no gender recorded means gender IS NULL. Empty-string genders are treated as recorded values.
If a gender group has zero total orders, its customers' share is NULL. The average share ignores those NULLs, and those customers cannot pass the above-average filter.
The average share is the unweighted mean of per-customer shares over all customers with a gender, taken across all genders together.
